newsitem.title: USA: USDA promises decision soon on CRP acreage.
newsitem.headline: USDA promises decision soon on CRP acreage.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department will act soon to sign up acreage for the Conservation Reserve Program, USDA Secretary Dan Glickman said Wednesday.
"I haven't made the decisions yet which will then allow the notices to go out. But it will be soon," Glickman told reporters following a speech to an Asian-Pacific group.
The agency faces a deadline at the end of the month for decisions on the CRP, and Glickman said it "might even beat that by a few days."

Last week, Glickman announced that a second CRP sign-up would be held later this year. The action came after 14 senators from farm states complained that the USDA decision on acreage acceptance would come too late for farmers who had to begin field preparation several weeks ago.
USDA previously indicated it might accept up to 19 million acres of the 25.6 million acres offered by farmers during the March sign-up period.
The CRP program pays farmers to stop production from fields that are environmentally sensitive.
